text.p: Germany's electronics giant Siemens AG said Thursday its first-quarter earnings fell 5 percent to 478 million German marks ($284 million) despite strong growth in orders and sales.
However, the company predicted steady profits and faster growth than previously expected in sales and orders in the fiscal year ending on Sept. 30.
Speaking to shareholders in Berlin, Siemens Chairman Heinrich von Pierer said the fall in profits in the quarter ended in December was a temporary dent.

"We expect sales and orders to exceed the somewhat muted original forecast for the year. The present favourable currency situation and the low interest level are largely responsible for this unforeseen growth," he said.

"In the past three years we continually improved our results. We will reach last year's high 2.5 billion marks ($1.5 billion) level again this year. And next year, we anticipate another increase," he added.
The company's sales and orders for the first quarter rose sharply on the back of favourable foreign exchange markets and low German interest rates.
Incoming orders surged 22 percent to 27 billion marks ($16.0 billion) and sales rose 6 percent to 20.9 billion marks ($12.4 billion).
Of the total, domestic orders rose 8 billion to 9.5 billion marks ($4.8 billion to $5.6 billion) and foreign orders soared 31 percent to 17.5 billion marks ($10.4 billion).
